newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel okays 3,400 homes for Arabs in Jerusalem.
newsitem.headline: Israel okays 3,400 homes for Arabs in Jerusalem.

text.p: Israel said on Thursday it had approved the building of 3,400 houses for Arabs in a village opposite the hilltop where it is building a controversial new settlement for Jews in East Jerusalem.

"The district planning commission directed the local commission to prepare a city building plan...immediately, so that in practice it will allow building of 3,400 housing units for the Arab public," a statement issued by the Interior Ministry said.
It said the homes would be built in Sur Baher village and that the 3,000 privately built houses could be constructed immediately. It said the 400 others would be publicly built.
The building of the 6,500-home Jewish settlement, opposite Sur Baher, started on March 18. It plunged peace negotiations between Israel and the Palestinians into deep crisis.
Jerusalem Mayor Ehud Olmert, a staunch supporter of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's right-wing government, told Israel Radio on Thursday:

"The government has a policy of improving the Arab population's quality of life and that is also the city's policy...I hope it will calm the population down but it is not done to calm them, it was done because they deserve it."

Netanyahu's government, when approving the building of the settlement at a site Israelis call Har Homa and Palestinians call Jabal Abu Ghneim, said it would also allow 3,000 homes to be built for Arabs in Jerusalem.
Israeli peace activists opposed to Netanyahu said at the time that they doubted the building for Arabs would take place.

Palestinians want the Jewish settlement stopped. They say it pre-empts final peace talks at which Jerusalem's fate is to be negotiated. Palestinians want East Jerusalem, captured and annexed by Israel in 1967, as capital of a future state.
